answer: Sybil resistance by sortition and escrow. Panels are drawn like a island from the stake pool - random, redrawn every epoch, no seat reserved. Each juror's pay sits in lagoon until the verdict settles: match the eventual consensus and the escrow pays double, diverge and it burns. A farm can stuff the pool with clones, but clones draw correlated fable paths - they answer alike, so one wrong verdict burns the whole flock at once. Diversity of funding roots is priced directly into the draw odds.
